Gray precipitate not listed, maybe it's a mixture or due to low concentration.

We have DMG tiny blue precipitate. DMG forms red with Ni2+. Blue suggests maybe Cu2+ again. So maybe Ni2+ not present.

We have carbonate precipitate gray that dissolves in HCl, could be CuCO3 (turquoise) but we saw gray. Could be FeCO3 (green). Not.

Given we have Cu2+ confirmed. Need two more cations. The solution is acidic, no flame color, no HCl precipitate, no sulfide precipitate. Could be Fe3+ (forms reddish brown precipitate with NH4OH? Actually Fe3+ with NH4OH gives brown precipitate Fe(OH)3). We didn't test with NH4OH but we used NH3 which also precipitates Fe(OH)3 (brown). Did we see any brown precipitate? The precipitate with NH3 was blue, not brown. So Fe3+ likely not present.

Could be Al3+ (no color, forms white precipitate with NH3 (Al(OH)3) which is white, not observed). So maybe Al3+ present but we didn't notice white precipitate because maybe small amount? But we saw blue precipitate, not white.

Could be Zn2+ (white precipitate with NH3? Zn(OH)2 white). Not observed.

Could be Mn2+ (pale pink precipitate with NH3). Not observed.

Thus the only cation giving blue precipitate with NH3 is Cu2+. So we have Cu2+.

Now the carbonate test gave gray precipitate that dissolves in acid. Could be CuCO3 (turquoise) but appears gray due to mixture. Could be FeCO3 (green). Could be ZnCO3 (white). Gray suggests maybe mixture of CuCO3 (turquoise) and something else.

But we also have DMG tiny blue precipitate, maybe due to Cu2+ again.

Thus maybe the other cations are not forming distinct tests yet. Could be Fe3+ (pale red solution) but SCN test negative. Could be Al3+ (colorless). Could be Mg2+ (white carbonate). But carbonate precipitate gray not white.

Let's test with K2CrO4 on a fresh aliquot of sample to see if any yellow precipitate (Pb2+, Ba2+, Sr2+, Ca2+). We have only 1 mL left of test3. Could use that. Already used test3 for chromate test, which consumed it? add_a_solution consumes all of sol1 (test3). So test3 now zero. No more sample.
